assertion: The seasonally adjusted delinquency rate for one- to four-unit residential properties was up 5 basis points from the second quarter and 43 bps from a year earlier [to 4.42%].
independent_value: MBA Q3 2025: 3.99%; HousingWire Q2 2026: 4.37%; Scotsman Guide copy of MBA release: 4.42%, +5 q/q, +43 y/y.
measure: mortgage delinquency rate MBA National Delinquency Survey
reason: No warehouse table carries the MBA NDS; NY Fed series in econ.household_debt_credit corroborates direction (mortgage 90+ day 0.83 to 1.13).

assertion: The percentage of loans already in foreclosure reached 0.71%, up 4 bps quarterly and 21 bps year over year; foreclosure starts rose 1 bp to 0.21%.
The 30-day rate increased 4 basis points to 2.25%, the 60-day rate rose 1 bps to 0.74%, and the 90-day delinquency rate remained unchanged at 1.43%.
The conventional rate increased 1 bp to 2.73%, FHA declined 5 bps to 11.74%, VA rose 11 bps to 5%; annual increases of 11, 96 and 50 bps.

The seriously delinquent rate reached 2.12% nonseasonally adjusted, up 6 basis points from the second quarter and 51 bps year over year; loans 90+ days late or in foreclosure increased for the fifth consecutive quarter.
The FHA foreclosure rate reached 1.89%, its highest level since the first quarter of 2017, while the VA foreclosure rate climbed to 1.06%, its highest since Q4 2016.
independent_value: Quoted from MBA release in Scotsman Guide copy; the long historical series is not in the warehouse, so the 'since' dates rest on MBA's statement.

assertion: FHA loans recorded the largest annual deterioration in serious delinquencies, with the rate rising 197 basis points. The rate increased 13 basis points for conventional loans and 60 basis points for VA loans.
reason: Scotsman Guide and HousingWire Q2 2026 were read; neither carries the Q3 2026 serious-delinquency-by-loan-type figures. Q2 2026 (FHA +227, conv +6, VA +31) is directionally consistent but a different quarter.
why_no_page: MBA's Q3 2026 release was not indexed or fetchable; Scotsman Guide and HousingWire Q2 loaded but lack these figures.
searched: MBA National Delinquency Survey Q3 2026 serious delinquency FHA 197 basis points

assertion: The five states with the largest quarterly increases in overall mortgage delinquencies were Wyoming, up 72 basis points, followed by West Virginia and Louisiana, both up 32 basis points. Arkansas saw its rate increase by 31 basis points, while Kentucky's rose by 27 bps.
independent_value: Scotsman Guide's MBA-sourced list is identical.

assertion: Walsh said the overall mortgage delinquency rate closely tracks the national unemployment rate, which stood at 4.1% in October.
speaker: Marina Walsh
inaccuracy: The 4.1% October figure is right, but the claim says delinquency closely tracks unemployment; over the past year unemployment fell (4.4% Sep 2025 to 4.2% Sep 2026) while MBA delinquency rose 43 bps, so the recent data diverge.
why_not: The fetched HousingWire jobs article confirms the 4.1% October unemployment figure, which I graded as correct; the partial-false grade rests on the 'closely tracks' part, which that article does not address (it says unemployment is lower than last year).
sql: SELECT date,value FROM econ.fred_indicators WHERE series='UNRATE' AND date>='2025-06-01' ORDER BY date

assertion: Walsh pointed to wage growth lagging inflation, declining personal savings, and rising balances on credit cards, auto loans and student loans.
speaker: Marina Walsh
warehouse_value: Avg hourly earnings Sep 2026 37.86 vs 36.70 = +3.2% y/y; CPI-U 336.94 vs 324.8 = +3.7%; saving rate 5.1% to 3.8%; NY Fed 90+ day delinquent: auto 5.02 to 5.66, student 9.36 to 10.92, card 12.41 to 12.90
sql: SELECT date,value FROM econ.wage_growth WHERE series='CES0500000003'

assertion: Changes to mortgage relief programs over the past year, including the removal of some COVID-era flexibilities, could be adding to financial pressures for some homeowners.
speaker: Marina Walsh
reason: Hedged ('could'); consistent with MBA's Nov 2025 warning and NY Fed mortgage 90+ day delinquency rising 0.83 to 1.13.
sql: SELECT period,loan_type,value FROM econ.household_debt_credit WHERE metric='pct_balance_90plus_delinquent' AND loan_type='mortgage'
